diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let us assume that the outliers are chosen in such a way that at $\w_C$, all the outliers have the lowest loss.
Now, we can repeat the above analysis recursively for every corresponding $\w_C$ and $\tilde{\w}$ in the landscape
Following the above analysis recursively, we can show that all other subsequent bad local minimas are avoided as well

issues.failure_explanation: Stationarity at w̄ is sum_i p_i(w̄)∇f_i(w̄)=0, with weights at w̄. The proof instead writes it with weights p_i(w_C) at an auxiliary far point and solves for w̄ as a weighted mean. Only the single configuration where all outliers rank lowest is analysed, via the crossing point of the (l_m,l_M) pair. This is the first crossing, not the last one that defines B_r (all clean losses below all outlier losses). Every other ordering, i.e. all later local minima, is dismissed by an unelaborated 'repeat recursively'. The hypothesis q>0 involves θ_{M,w̄}, which depends on the stationary point being bounded, so the condition is circular. γ is defined as 2δ/max in the statement but as min/max in the proof, and the step treats a ratio inequality as equality.

failure_location.quote: Starting from any initialization $\w_0$, for any stationary point $\bar{\w}$ attained by \mkl, we have that $\bar{\w} \in \mathcal{B}_r(\ws)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum a proof must analyse stationarity with weights p(w̄) at w̄ itself, treat every rank configuration (not just the first bad minimum), place w̄ inside the region defined by the last crossing, and state a hypothesis that does not depend on the unknown w̄.
issues.overall_effect: The central landscape claim, that with Condition 1 / q>0 every stationary point lies in B_r(w*) from any initialization, is unsupported. So are the stated effects of κ, γ and θ on the tolerable outlier fraction.
issues.title: Proof of the no-bad-local-minima lemma conflates probabilities at w_C and at the stationary point, handles only the first bad minimum, and has a circular hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The stated guarantee is the paper's main structural result on outlier landscapes. Establishing it for all local minima needs a genuinely new argument and possibly a changed hypothesis, not a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \min\left(\epsilon n  G(\wsgd), (1 - \epsilon) n L \norm{\wsgd - \ws}\right)
we will assume that $\norm{\nabla f_i(\bs{w})} \leq G ~\forall~i\in \mathbb{O}$

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma claims a lower bound on SGD's error, ε G ≤ (1-ε) L ‖w̄_SGD - w*‖. The proof only establishes ‖Σ_O ∇f_i‖ ≤ εnG and ‖Σ_O ∇f_i‖ ≤ (1-ε)nL‖w̄-w*‖ (and drops a factor n). It then asserts the norm equals the min of the two upper bounds, which does not follow and does not give the claimed inequality. G is only an upper bound on outlier gradients. Counterexample: scalar equal-l quadratics give w̄_SGD=(1-ε)w*+εw_B and exact outlier gradient norm 2l(1-ε)|w_B-w*|. The claimed inequality then holds only if G equals that value, and fails for any larger valid upper bound G.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum a quantitative lower bound on SGD's error is needed, e.g. a lower bound on the outlier gradient sum at w̄_SGD with G redefined accordingly, together with a consistent role for G in the MKL upper bound.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 2 chains this inequality with the MKL bound, so the headline claim that MKL stationary points beat SGD's fixed point is not established.
issues.title: SGD lower-bound lemma is not supported: proof gives only upper bounds, and 'equality with min' is false
issues.why_classification: The SGD-vs-MKL comparison requires a lower bound on SGD error. The proof's tools give only upper bounds, so a new hypothesis and argument are needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Naively, $\lambda_{\w} = \min_i p_i(\w) \lambda$
Picking a large enough $k$, we can guarantee that
using larger $k$ (any $k < \dfrac{n}{2}$), reduces $\alpha(\epsilon, L, k, \lambda)$
Note, $p_{min}$ is a positive constant independent of $\w$

issues.failure_explanation: λ=min_w λ_w comes from Lemma 1 with weights p_i(w) given by the with-replacement formula, which depends on k; naively λ_w≥λ_F·min_i p_i ≥ λ_F/n^k. Then ε^k G/λ can be of order (nε)^k G/λ_F and α=(1-ε)Lε^{k-1}/λ of order (nε)^k, which does not tend to 0 (nor drop below 1) as k grows unless nε<1. The 'exists k' and 'larger k decreases α' arguments treat λ as a k-free constant. The same worst-ranked-clean-sample weight is about ε^k-scale, so numerator and denominator decay at comparable rates.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum a lower bound on λ_w with explicit k-dependence must be derived and k' / α redone (possibly under extra conditions such as stronger convexity of small subsets), with a correspondingly weaker regime of k.
issues.overall_effect: The claims that the MKL error bound vanishes with k, that α<1 for large k, and that increasing k inside B_r improves the guarantee are unsupported.
issues.title: Constant λ is treated as independent of k although it is built from k-dependent probabilities
issues.why_classification: Correcting the k-dependence changes the rate and may remove the large-k regime, which is the mechanism behind the comparison with SGD. A new quantitative lemma and a reoptimised or weakened theorem are required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\wsm$ be any first order stationary point attained by \mkl.
for any $\wsm \in \mathcal{B}_r(\ws)$ and $\lambda$ defined in equation

issues.failure_explanation: The last step replaces Σ_{i∈O} p_i(w̄) by ε^k. That value holds only when all outliers occupy the worst |O| ranks at w̄, i.e. w̄∈B_r. For a general stationary point the outlier mass can be as large as p̂_max=1-(1-ε)^k. The lemma is stated for any first-order stationary point, with no such hypothesis. It also uses the SGD-point bound G(w̄_SGD) for gradients at w̄_MKL without stating G is a uniform bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis w̄_MKL∈B_r(w*) to the lemma, as Theorem 2 already does, and state G as a uniform bound.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the lemma is false or unsupported for stationary points outside B_r; Theorem 2 adds the B_r hypothesis itself, so its use is unaffected.
issues.title: MKL error bound stated for any stationary point but proof needs outliers ranked worst (w̄ in B_r)
issues.why_classification: Adding the already-used hypothesis fixes the statement without changing any claim or proof structure.

for any $\wsm \in \mathcal{B}_r(\ws)$ and $\lambda$ defined in equation

issues.failure_explanation: The text claims a worst-case guarantee over all MKL stationary points. Theorem 2 only treats stationary points already inside B_r(w*). The paper itself says that without the Lemma 2 conditions MKL can get stuck at bad local minima near the outlier center, where no comparison with SGD is proved.

failure_location.quote: Finally, we show that any solution attained by \mkl~is provably better than the solution attained by SGD.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claim as applying only to stationary points in B_r(w*), and drop 'any' and 'even the worst solution' unless B_r membership is proved for all stationary points.

issues.title: Prose claims every MKL solution (even the worst) beats SGD, but the theorem covers only stationary points in B_r
issues.why_classification: The formal result survives but the headline worst-case guarantee must be withdrawn or restricted.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: 2\eta_t^2\sum_{i\in \mathcal{G}} p_i(\bs{w_t}) \norm{\nabla f_{i}( \wg)}^2
Theorem \ref{thm:R} implies that for any stochastic algorithm in the both noisy and noiseless setting

issues.failure_explanation: The proof (appendix theorem lem:R) produces the term 2η²Σ_{i∈G} p_i‖∇f_i(w*)‖² over good samples, and no ‖∇f_i(w*)‖² term over outliers. The main-text R_t drops the good-sample term and instead puts 2η‖∇f_i(w*)‖² on the outliers. In the noisy setting ∇f_i(w*)≠0 for good samples, so the omitted positive term makes the stated bound unproved and possibly false, although the text asserts it for both noisy and noiseless settings. The remark that R_t 'reduces' in the noiseless outlier case is derived from the mis-stated residual.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace R_t in the main theorem by the appendix expression, with the good-sample term over G and no extra outlier gradient term, and redo the accompanying discussion.
issues.overall_effect: The main-text theorem is not what is proved; its noisy-setting use and the residual-term discussion rest on the wrong expression.
issues.title: Main-text Distance-to-w* theorem states a residual different from what the proof yields, and fails in the noisy setting
issues.why_classification: The correct statement is already proved in the appendix; replacing the residual and adjusting the remarks is routine.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Term1 &\leq \min_{i}p_i(\bs{w_t})
Now we first bound $Term1$ as follows

issues.failure_explanation: Term1 enters with a negative coefficient in (contraction), so a lower bound is needed. The proof states 'Term1 ≤ min p · Σ⟨...⟩ ≤ min p · λ_good‖w_{t+1}-w*‖²'. Both steps have the wrong direction: since p_i≥min p and each inner product is nonnegative, the true relations are ≥. The final norm should be at w_t, not w_{t+1}. The strong-convexity step also needs the averaged F_good definition (a factor |G|) that is not reconciled.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace '≤' by '≥' in both steps, use ‖w_t-w*‖², and state the strong-convexity step with the correct normalisation.
issues.overall_effect: As written the contraction coefficient is not justified. The statement is repairable by reversing the inequalities.
issues.title: Wrong inequality direction (and w_{t+1}) when bounding Term1 in the distance-to-w* proof
issues.why_classification: The correct lower bound is short and gives the stated coefficient with a (weaker, safe) constant; no claim changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose we have $\abs{\mathcal{G}}\leq \frac{n}{2}$.

issues.failure_explanation: For MKL-2 the outlier at rank i has weight 2(n-i)/(n(n-1)). The proof bounds this by 1/n, which requires i≥(n+1)/2. Outliers occupy ranks |G|+1,...,n, so for |G|<(n-1)/2 the highest-ranked outliers have weight up to about 2/n>1/n. Their terms η²‖∇f_i(w_t)‖² and 2η(f_i(w*)-f_i(w_t)) are not ordered or signed, so the replacement is unjustified. The noise conditions only offset the good-sample terms, so R_t^{MKL2}≤R_t^{SGD} is not proved for most of the advertised regime |G|≤n/2 (it holds at best near |G|≈n/2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum the comparison must handle the non-uniform outlier weights, e.g. by restricting to |G|≥(n-1)/2 or adding assumptions that order or bound the outlier contribution terms.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that MKL-SGD beats SGD even when more than half the data is corrupted is not established for |G| well below n/2.
issues.title: Corollary compares MKL-2 and SGD residuals using an outlier-weight bound that fails when |G|<(n-1)/2
issues.why_classification: The advertised majority-outlier regime is not covered by the argument. Recovering it needs new assumptions or a different comparison, or the regime shrinks to almost nothing.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \sqrt{n\sum_{i\in \mathcal{G}} \|\nabla f_{i}( \wg)\|^2}

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs A ≥ 2√n·s·‖Δ‖ + η s², where s=(Σ‖∇f_i(w*)‖²)^{1/2} and A=(1-ηL)λ|G|/(n-1)·‖Δ‖². Solving the quadratic gives s ≤ A'/(√n+√(n+ηA')), with n inside the inner root. The stated threshold has √n there instead. For large n and η small, the stated threshold is about A/√n, roughly twice the admissible A/(2√n), so the stated condition does not imply the needed inequality (e.g. n=10^4 gives 2√n·c ≈ 1.8A>A).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the inner √n by n (and use the (n-1)/n normalisation consistently) in the second noise-level condition, then re-verify the displayed chain.
issues.overall_effect: The second noise-level alternative of the corollary is not a valid sufficient condition as stated.
issues.title: Noise-level condition (noise-level2) does not imply the required inequality: wrong square-root constant
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the quadratic root restores the alternative without changing the corollary's structure.
